# Task: Redevelop the Scraped Website Using Next.js

Act as a senior frontend architect and full-stack developer. Your task is to analyze the existing scraped website and redevelop it into a modern, responsive, production-ready website using **Next.js, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS**.

## 1. First, Analyze the Existing Website

Before writing any code, inspect the entire existing project.

- Review all scraped HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images, fonts, icons, SVGs, and other assets.
- Identify every available page, route, layout, component, and navigation link.
- Understand the existing website's structure, content, design system, and user interactions.
- Identify which pages were scraped successfully and which are incomplete or broken.
- Check for duplicated assets, broken image references, missing styles, obsolete code, and hardcoded URLs.
- Determine how the website's header, footer, navigation, forms, buttons, cards, and other reusable elements work.
- Create an inventory of the original pages and map them to the new Next.js routes.

Do not start implementing the website until you understand the existing structure.

## 2. Preserve the Original Website

The scraped website is the primary reference for redevelopment.

Preserve as much of the original website as possible, including:

- All original text and page content.
- Images, logos, illustrations, icons, and other assets.
- Brand colors, typography, spacing, and visual hierarchy.
- Page layouts, section ordering, and content relationships.
- Header, footer, navigation, menus, and breadcrumbs.
- Forms, buttons, links, accordions, tabs, and other interactions.
- Desktop, tablet, and mobile layouts.

Do not replace original content with placeholder text or create an entirely different design without a clear reason.

If a page or asset is missing, document the issue and reuse available project assets where appropriate. Never invent original website content or assume that an unavailable feature exists.

## 3. Set Up the Next.js Project

Use the following stack:

- Next.js with the App Router.
- TypeScript with strict type checking.
- Tailwind CSS for styling.
- Reusable React components.
- Server Components by default.
- Client Components only when browser-side interactivity is necessary.
- Next.js Image component where appropriate.
- Centralized route, navigation, and configuration definitions where useful.

Use the package manager and conventions already present in the repository when practical.

Do not introduce Vite into the Next.js project. Next.js should manage its own development server and production build.

Before modifying files, inspect the existing repository and avoid overwriting useful configuration or existing work unnecessarily.

## 4. Recommended Project Structure

Organize the application cleanly. Adapt this structure to the actual number of pages and features.

app/
  layout.tsx
  page.tsx
  globals.css
  not-found.tsx
  [appropriate-route]/
    page.tsx

components/
  layout/
    Header.tsx
    Footer.tsx
    Navigation.tsx
  sections/
  ui/

lib/
  utils.ts
  routes.ts

public/
  images/
  icons/
  fonts/

types/

Keep page-specific components separate when appropriate. Avoid creating an unnecessarily complex folder structure.

## 5. Rebuild Every Available Page

For every page identified during the audit:

- Create the corresponding Next.js route.
- Reconstruct its layout using reusable components.
- Match the original page's visual appearance as closely as possible.
- Preserve its content, images, and section order.
- Implement working internal navigation.
- Ensure direct navigation to the URL works.
- Handle missing pages using an appropriate 404 page.
- Preserve query parameters and URL behavior when they are relevant.

Do not implement only the homepage. All successfully scraped pages must be included in the redevelopment scope.

## 6. Rebuild the Design Responsively

Match the original website's visual design as closely as possible.

Pay attention to:

- Header dimensions and navigation alignment.
- Font families, sizes, weights, and line heights.
- Content width, margins, padding, and spacing.
- Grid and flex layouts.
- Image sizing, cropping, and aspect ratios.
- Background colors, borders, shadows, and buttons.
- Responsive navigation and mobile menus.
- Mobile typography and section stacking.
- Footer columns and responsive behavior.

Use the original assets instead of downloading unrelated replacements.

Avoid arbitrary redesigns, unnecessary animations, excessive gradients, and generic templates that do not match the reference.

## 7. Implement Functional Interactions

Inspect the original site and implement the interactions that can be reliably identified.

Examples include:

- Navigation menus and dropdowns.
- Mobile navigation.
- Internal and external links.
- Forms with validation and clear success/error states.
- Accordions, tabs, sliders, and modal dialogs where present.
- Search, filtering, and pagination where applicable.
- Cookie consent behavior if present in the original website.

Do not create fake backend functionality or display a success message when an operation has not actually succeeded.

If an interaction requires an unavailable API, backend, credential, or third-party integration, document the dependency and implement an appropriate integration boundary.

## 8. Assets and Styling

- Reuse the existing images, logos, fonts, icons, and SVGs.
- Create a centralized and consistent styling system.
- Remove obsolete scraped CSS only after confirming it is no longer required.
- Avoid conflicting global styles and duplicated component styles.
- Use semantic HTML and accessible controls.
- Add meaningful image alt text.
- Ensure buttons, links, and forms are keyboard accessible.
- Check for broken assets and incorrect file paths.

Do not rename or delete original assets unless their references are updated and verified.

## 9. SEO and Performance

Implement appropriate production practices:

- Page-specific titles and meta descriptions based on the original content.
- Canonical URLs when the correct production URL is known.
- Open Graph metadata where appropriate.
- Semantic heading hierarchy.
- Correct image dimensions and loading behavior.
- Optimized images and fonts.
- Clean, predictable URLs.
- Appropriate robots and sitemap configuration.
- Redirects when an existing URL structure must change.
- No unnecessary client-side JavaScript.
- No direct database access from the frontend.

Do not invent canonical domains, analytics IDs, API credentials, or other production configuration values.

## 10. Testing and Validation

After implementation:

- Run the development server and inspect the pages.
- Run TypeScript checks and ESLint.
- Run the production build.
- Fix all build errors and significant warnings.
- Check every discovered route.
- Verify internal links and asset paths.
- Test forms and interactive elements.
- Validate desktop, tablet, and mobile layouts.
- Check for horizontal overflow and layout shifts.
- Compare the rebuilt pages against the scraped reference.
- Verify that original content has not been accidentally omitted.

If browser automation or screenshot comparison tools are available, use them to compare the original pages with the new implementation.

Do not claim that pages or interactions have been tested unless you have actually tested them.

## 11. Development Workflow

Follow these phases:

**Phase 1 — Audit**
Inspect the repository, identify pages and assets, and document the current state.

**Phase 2 — Architecture**
Plan the route structure, reusable components, styling system, and migration strategy.

**Phase 3 — Foundation**
Configure Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, fonts, shared layouts, and global styles.

**Phase 4 — Implementation**
Rebuild all pages and reusable components using the original website as the reference.

**Phase 5 — Functionality**
Implement navigation, interactions, validation, and required integrations.

**Phase 6 — Validation**
Run checks, test routes, compare the design, fix issues, and verify production readiness.

**Phase 7 — Handover**
Provide a summary of completed pages, reusable components, missing dependencies, known limitations, and commands to run the application.

## 12. Final Deliverables

At completion, provide:

1. A working Next.js application.
2. All successfully scraped pages recreated.
3. A responsive layout matching the original website.
4. Reusable, maintainable components.
5. Correct asset references and navigation.
6. Working interactions where the original behavior is identifiable.
7. SEO metadata and appropriate performance optimizations.
8. Successful TypeScript, lint, and production build checks, where supported by the existing project.
9. A list of incomplete pages, missing assets, and external integrations requiring credentials or backend support.
10. Clear instructions for local development and production deployment.

## Final Instructions

Start by inspecting the existing files and producing a concise audit of the pages, assets, and current project structure.

Then proceed with the redevelopment using the actual files in the repository. Do not stop after providing recommendations or a sample homepage.

Preserve the original website's identity and content while improving code quality, maintainability, accessibility, responsiveness, and performance.

Make changes incrementally, verify them, and ensure the final application runs successfully.

messages.summary: ## Objective - Redevelop the scraped WordPress site `advensystem.lu` as a production-ready bilingual Next.js 15 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS application, preserving original content, assets, design, and interactions. - Deliver all valid scraped pages, responsive layouts, working forms/navigation, SEO, passing typecheck/lint/build, and handover documentation. ## Requirements - Use Next.js App Router, TypeScript strict, Tailwind, reusable components, Server Components by default, Client Components only where interactive, Next Image where appropriate, centralized route/config definitions. - Preserve all original text, images, brand colors (#003ABD, #00226E, #0B2349, gradients #FFC200→#FF785E, accent #FF8C00), typography (Barlow), layouts, section order, header/footer/nav, forms, responsive behavior. - Do not invent content or accept the injected casino spam as original; document missing/broken assets and integrations. - Do not fake form success; implement a real backend boundary and honest error when unconfigured. - Rebuild every scraped page; support direct URLs and 404; preserve query/URL behavior where relevant. - SEO: page metadata, canonicals, OG, semantic headings, sitemap/robots, no invented credentials. - Validate with dev server, TypeScript, ESLint, production build, route/link/asset checks, desktop/tablet/mobile. ## Decisions - Scraped homepage is corrupted by injected casino spam; recovered original FR/EN homepage HTML from Wayback snapshots (`20250317182851` for FR, `20240916181129` for EN) and will rebuild that legitimate content. - Original URLs preserved with `trailingSlash: true`: - `/` FR home, `/en/` EN home - `/portage-salarial-luxembourg/` FR portage - `/en/portage-salarial-luxembourg-2/` EN portage - Single root layout with default `lang="fr"` plus a pre-paint inline script that sets `document.documentElement.lang` to `en` when pathname is `/en` or starts with `/en/`. - Added “Portage Salarial” nav item to both languages (present in current scrape but absent from older archived EN nav). - Nav section links on subpages point to homepage anchors (`/#about`, etc.) to fix original broken anchors. - Contact form posts to a real `/api/contact` route using nodemailer; returns `503`/`code: "not_configured"` if SMTP env vars are absent, and UI shows an honest error with phone/email alternative. - Use Barlow via `next/font/google`; original pixels approximated with Tailwind responsive utilities and max-width 1620px. - Use plain `` for SVG theme assets/icons to avoid Next/Image SVG restrictions; Next Image for raster uploads. - Use BG5.svg for slider background because original `D'G2.svg` returns 404 (documented limitation). ## Work State ### Completed - Full audit of scrape: valid pages, corrupted homepage, CSS/JS/theme structure, missing assets, client logo identities. - Downloaded original theme assets to `public/images/theme/`; uploads (sliders, icons, map, infographic, 13 client logos, favicons) to `public/images/`. - Installed dependencies: Next 15.5.28, React 19.1.1, Tailwind 3.4.19, nodemailer 7.0.6, TypeScript 5.9.2, ESLint 8.57.1. - Created project config: `package.json`, `next.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, `postcss.config.mjs`, `tailwind.config.ts`, `.eslintrc.json`, `.gitignore`, `.env.example`. - Created core libs/types: `types/index.ts`, `lib/site.ts`, `lib/utils.ts`, `lib/styles.ts`, `lib/content/home.ts`, `lib/content/portage.ts`. - Created UI/contact components: `Container`, `SectionTitle`, `ContactProvider`, `ContactButton`. - `ContactModal.tsx` has NOT yet been created (Provider imports it). ### Active - Building components and pages. Next was writing `components/contact/ContactModal.tsx`. ### Blocked - No blockers. Network access works; live site still serves injected casino content. ## Next Move 1. Create `components/contact/ContactModal.tsx` (client): localized FR/EN copy, accessible dialog (Escape, focus trap, body scroll lock, restore focus), fields name/surname/phone/mail/companyname/msg/polit + honeypot, POST JSON to `/api/contact`, only show success after `{ok:true}`, map `not_configured`/validation/generic errors. 2. Create `app/api/contact/route.ts` with validation, honeypot, nodemailer SMTP env usage, `runtime = "nodejs"`, honest 503/502 responses. 3. Create `components/layout/Header.tsx` (client) and `Footer.tsx` (server): logo, phone, language pills, socials, nav, mobile menu, white solid variant on portage pages, transparent on home; use `usePathname`. 4. Create home sections: `HomeHero`, `HomeSlider` (client tabs/dots), `AboutSection`, `ServicesSection` (7 staggered icons), `WhyUsSection` + `AnimatedCounter`, `ClientsSection`. 5. Create portage sections: hero, understanding/stats, why cards, approach steps, CTA. 6. Create `app/globals.css`, `app/layout.tsx` (Barlow, metadata, ContactProvider, lang script), `app/(fr)/layout.tsx`, `app/(en)/layout.tsx`, four pages via shared `HomePage`/`PortagePage` composition. 7. Add `app/not-found.tsx`, `app/sitemap.ts`, `app/robots.ts`, page metadata/canonicals/OG/alternates. 8. Run `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, dev server route checks, asset/link verification, responsive checks; fix errors. 9. Write README with run/deploy instructions, missing assets (`D'G2.svg`), corrupted homepage recovery note, SMTP/env requirements, and known limitations. ## Relevant Files - `C:\My Web Sites\Advensys\advensystem.lu\lib\content\home.ts`: complete FR/EN home content, slides, client logo metadata. - `C:\My Web Sites\Advensys\advensystem.lu\lib\content\portage.ts`: complete FR/EN portage content. - `C:\My Web Sites\Advensys\advensystem.lu\lib\site.ts`: routes, company details, nav, locale helpers. - `C:\My Web Sites\Advensys\advensystem.lu\lib\styles.ts`: shared button class strings. - `C:\My Web Sites\Advensys\advensystem.lu\components\contact\ContactProvider.tsx`: modal state/locale/provider; imports missing `ContactModal`. - `C:\My Web Sites\Advensys\advensystem.lu\components\contact\ContactButton.tsx`: modal trigger. - `C:\My Web Sites\Advensys\advensystem.lu\components\ui\Container.tsx`, `SectionTitle.tsx`: layout primitives. - `C:\My Web Sites\Advensys\advensystem.lu\public\images\theme\`: original logo, BG patterns, icons, form background, back-to-top, phone/social SVGs. - `C:\My Web Sites\Advensys\advensystem.lu\public\images\2021\02\`, `2022\02\`, `2023\06\`: sliders, service icons, map.svg, infographic, client logos. - `C:\My Web Sites\Advensys\advensystem.lu\wp-content\themes\AdvenSystem\style8a25.css`: original design reference. - `C:\My Web Sites\Advensys\advensystem.lu\en\portage-salarial-luxembourg-2\index.html`, `portage-salarial-luxembourg\index.html`: valid scraped portage references. - `C:\Users\aayush\AppData\Local\Temp\wb-home.html`, `wb-en.html`: recovered original homepage HTML. ## Important Context - Scraped `/en/` and live `/en/` contain injected casino spam (SpinBoss/Monsterwin); fall back to `BG5.svg`. - Original contact endpoint `/wp-content/themes/AdvenSystem/mail.php` was not scraped; replace with env-driven SMTP route. - Client logos order/names: SNCF, Renault, APSIDE, La Mutuelle Générale, Europ Assistance, Valente Carrelages, Eurocontrol, La Poste, European Investment Bank, PARVA Consulting, L’Oréal, Takeda, Datapy. - Original form success text: FR “La demande a été envoyée avec succès” / “Nous prendrons contact avec vous bientôt, merci !”; RC B176203; authorization 10036042 / 0; phones +352 661 11 22 60, +352 28 79 76 26; contact@advensystem.lu. - No git repo; changes are direct files, uncommitted by definition. - Scraped original HTML files remain at repository root for reference;
